title: [recoverability] Every engine is refused its passfile by name or variable, and 108's `ps x` and `top -c` globs are anchored on a command position (rev-e's N3)
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 113 [recoverability]: every engine is refused its passfile, by name or by its variable, and the two process-listing globs of 108 that refused ordinary commands are anchored on a command position.

Read CREDENTIAL_DENY in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs, as 108 leaves it.

Why.
- A passfile that engines hold through PGPASSFILE, under ~/.config/spawn/, is refused by its path (`*.config/spawn*`), but `cat $PGPASSFILE` names only the variable. It must be refused before any engine holds one (110, or what replaces it). `*.pgpass*` covers ~/.pgpass and any file of that name.
- rev-e's N3 on 108: `*ps x*` refused `ls groups x`, `cargo test -- steps x` and `jq '.ps x'`, and `*top *-c*` refused `systemctl --user stop x; sh -c true`. A false refusal costs a fleet turn and teaches agents to route around the list.

Required behaviour. CREDENTIAL_DENY:
- no longer holds `Bash(*ps x*)` or `Bash(*top *-c*)`;
- holds, exactly:
  - `Bash(ps x*)`, `Bash(*; ps x*)`, `Bash(*&& ps x*)`, `Bash(*| ps x*)`, `Bash(*$(ps x*)`;
  - the same five for `top *-c*`;
  - `Bash(*PGPASSFILE*)` and `Bash(*.pgpass*)`;
  - `Read(~/.pgpass)` and `Edit(~/.pgpass)`, so Claude Code's file tools are refused ~/.pgpass as Bash is (rev-e's F1 on 113). The passfile 110 plans is under ~/.config/spawn, which `Read(~/.config/spawn/**)` and `Edit(~/.config/spawn/**)` already cover.
That is, `ps x` and `top … -c` are refused at the start of a command, and after `; `, `&& `, `| ` and `$(`. Every other entry of 108 stays.
False refusals that remain, rare:
- `top … ` followed later in the same command by `-c` in another command, when the command starts with top;
- any command mentioning PGPASSFILE or .pgpass, even `echo $PGPASSFILE`, and `grep -rn PGPASSFILE crates/` while 110's own work reads the code: engines need not name it at run time, since libpq and spawn read it themselves; a search of the code uses the editor's search tools (Grep), which these rules do not refuse.
Not refused on the whole text: `ps x` after `||`, a newline, `(` or a backtick. Claude Code's per-part check covers the first two; the last two are open, as `$(` was before this objective.

This contract also changes 108.sh, where 113 replaces 108's rules: its entry list drops `Bash(*ps x*)` and `Bash(*top *-c*)` (139 entries), and its header says so. 108's refused commands `ps x`, `ps axww` and `top -b -n 1 -c` are still refused, by the anchored forms and `*ps ax*`.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs only. About 20 lines.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/113.sh (108's harness).
(1) Every engine's deny list holds the 14 entries exactly, and no longer holds the two old globs.
(2) Matched as Claude Code documents its Bash rules, the list refuses 16 commands on their whole text (the passfile by variable, ~/.pgpass and path; `ps x` and `top -c` at each command position) and none of 9 others (rev-e's four false refusals, `pgrep -f`, `ps -p`, `top -b -n 1`, psql naming $SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_URL, `cargo test`), whole or in any part. The commands are text: none is run. (2)'s matcher is Claude Code's Bash rules only; the Read and Edit entries are checked by (1).
108.sh (as changed) must keep passing. check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass.
The limit of the check is as 108's: it reads the list handed to a fake engine, and does not watch a real engine refuse a command.
